game: TB @ BUF, 2025-11-16 13:00 ET, outdoor, BUF -6, total 46.5

script.base: Market script is Buffalo leading a moderate outdoor game (implied BUF 26.2 / TB 20.2, not a shootout and not a slog). Buffalo should be in front by a score by the second half and lean on James Cook late (59 carries, 383 yards in weeks 8-10). Tampa, a 6-point dog, throws more than it wants: Egbuka (34 targets) and Otton (26) stay involved, while White/Tucker carries shrink if the lead gets to two scores.
script.flip1: Tampa hangs around or leads behind the short game (Otton/Egbuka) and Buffalo's leaky run defense (5.54 YPC, 40 runs of 10+). Allen stays in pass mode, Cook's clock-killing carries never come, and both passing games clear in a 46.5-or-over script.
script.flip2: Buffalo jumps out early. Cook's late snaps get shared with Ray Davis, Tampa abandons the run (White/Tucker rush lines die), and Tampa's dropbacks rise but efficiency falls if Buffalo sits on the ball. A true blowout is not the base at only -6, but it is the snap-risk flip.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location splits only: BUF allows YPA left 6.99 (94), middle 7.3 (37), right 6.71 (113). TB allows left 5.71 (115), middle 9.25 (57), right 8.17 (136). Tampa's middle is the clear pass soft spot; Buffalo's pass YPA is ordinary.
matchup.pressure: BUF blitzes 31%; TB EPA/db is -0.24 when blitzed vs +0.29 when not, so heat kills Tampa's dropback and should force quick throws. TB blitzes 38%; BUF EPA/db is still +0.06 vs blitz and +0.32 with no blitz, so Allen is not blitz-fragile. Reddick out further lowers Tampa's pass-rush teeth. Bredeson out raises the chance Buffalo's 31% blitz actually gets home.
matchup.bleeds: BUF bleeds the run: 5.54 YPC and 40 runs of 10+ in 9 games, with only 26 passes of 20+ (269 yards). TB bleeds the pass, especially the middle (9.25 YPA) and right (8.17), plus 29 passes of 20+ for 334 yards; the run defense is the better unit at 4.25 YPC and 19 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: Tampa's primary target, Egbuka, is a deep-air profile (418 air yards, only 208 receiving) attacking the part of Buffalo that does not bleed, and he is the player most exposed to blitz plus a missing guard. The overlap that fits is Otton's short air (121 on 26 targets) into a pressure script, and Shakir's underneath role (74 air yards on 24 targets) into Tampa's 9.25 middle. Cook's 6.49 YPC heater runs into the stronger side of Tampa's defense, not the bleed.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. Buffalo's 5.54 YPC run defense let White and Tucker control tempo, Tampa's implied 20.2 came on the ground, and Otton repeated the 40-yard floor because Mayfield never needed eight targets. On the other side Tampa blitzed at 38%, Allen checked down to Knox and Hawes instead of Shakir, and a second-half lead turned the fourth quarter into Cook carries, so Shakir landed on the 33-yard side of his last four. The counter is real on both, stronger on Shakir than on Otton, and it is why Shakir stays a lean and why neither leg is sized without a price.
slip_story: One story only: a competitive BUF -6 game in the 26-20 band, not a blowout and not a paired total under. Dog throw volume to Otton, favorite underneath volume to Shakir with Kincaid out. They win together if both offenses function and lose together in a rock fight. Do not add Cook rush over (needs the clock-kill flip and a spike past a 4.25 YPC defense), Egbuka yards over (deep air into a non-bleed plus a missing guard), or any TD. Two legs, one market each, no depth receivers.
